1. The present revision petition has been preferred by the revisionist under Section 397 of Criminal Procedure (hereinafter referred to as 'Cr.PC') against the order dated 11.10.2023 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Impugned Order') passed by Ld. Metropolitan Magistrate, Mahila Court-03, West Mohit Chaudhary vs State on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143274493/
1 District, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi (herein after referred to as the 'Ld. Trial Court') in case CC No.
5641/2019, titled as State v. Mohit Chaudhary & others, whereby charge for the offence under Section 498A/34 IPC against all revisionists, under Section 406/34 IPC against revisionist Mohit,
Devraj (FIL) & Sheetal (MIL) and under Section 377 against revisionist Mohit and Section 354/354A against the revisionist Devraj (FIL) was directed to be framed.

Arguments addressed by revisionist :
2. Assailing the impugned order, revisionist submitted that the impugned order passed by the Ld.Trial Court is erroneous, based on surmises and conjectures and contrary to Law; the Ld.Trial Court while passing the impugned order has ignored the material statements, documents, facts and evidence on record; the Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate the facts that no allegations with respect to 354, 354A and 377 Cr.P.c. has been made by the complainant against the petitioners in the Petition u/s 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act; that the Criminal Revision No. 29/2024 prosecution has failed to place any documentary evidence on record to show that the petitioners had ever sought money from the complainant; that the complainant admittedly stayed for 14 days in her matrimonial home in Amritsar and shifted to Mohali and finally to Delhi, near her parent's home;
that the alleged version of complainant's mother to the petitioner no.3 is a gross improvement and in contradiction with the allegations contained in para 14 of the petition dated 06.08.2016 under Section 9 of HMA; that there is neither any medical evidence nor any police complaint of such incidents, spanning over a period of two years during the year 2014 to 2015 and the same has also been mentioned in the charge-sheet; that had there been any truthfulness in allegations relation to offences u/s 498A/406/354/377 IPC, in the year 2014 and 2015, she would neither have filed a petition under Section 9 of HMA, for restitution of Conjugal Rights nor went into mediation several times asking for exorbitant amount; that there are gross contradictions in the version of the complainant, in so far as allegation of entrustment of jewellery is concerned; that there is no incriminating evidence against the petitioners attracting the offences in question and the allegations in the FIR based on second complaint are absolutely atrocious, improbable, unreliable,
contradictory and gross improvements, besides being concocted and false on the face of it and that the complainant has dragged the entire family of her husband in the matrimonial dispute by making omnibus allegations of demand of dowry and assault, even though they were not residing with her in the matrimonial home.
hence, the present revision has been filed.

sentences.text: Per contra, Ld. Addl. PP for the State supporting the Impugned Order argued that there is no infirmity and illegality done by the Ld. Trial Court and has rightly passed the order on charge and framed charges against the accused persons under the relevant sections, hence, no interference of this Court is required.
Analysis and relevant law 5.

The Court heard the arguments as advanced by revisionists and Ld. Addl. PP for the State and have gone through the material available on record including the Trial Court Record.
6. Section 227 and 228 Cr. PC empowers a Judge to frame charge or discharge accused for the offence.

Before proceedings further, this Court deems it appropriate to reproduce both sections,
Criminal Revision No. 29/2024 which reads as under:
"227. Discharge.
If, upon consideration of the record of the case and the documents submitted therewith, and after hearing the submissions of the accused and the prosecution in this behalf, the Judge considers that there is not sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused, he shall discharge the accused and record his reasons for so doing."
228. Framing of charge.

(1) If, after such consideration and hearing as aforesaid, the Judge is of opinion that there is ground for presuming that the accused has committed an offence which-(a) is not exclusively triable by the Court of Session, he may, frame a charge against the accused and, by order, transfer the case for trial to the Chief Judicial Magistrate, and thereupon the Chief Judicial Magistrate shall try the offence in accordance with the procedure for the trial of warrant-cases instituted on a police report;(b) is exclusively triable by the Court, he shall frame in writing a charge against the accused.(2) Where the Judge frames any charge under clause (b) of sub-section (1), the charge shall be read and explained to the accused and the accused shall be asked whether he pleads guilty of the offence charged or claims to be tried."
7. Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Sajjan Kumar v. CBI reported in (2010) 9 SCC 368, has laid down the principles on the scope of Section 227 and 228 of Cr.P.C., which read as under:
Criminal Revision No. 29/2024 "21.

entities.text: Sajjan Kumar v. CBI reported in (2010) 9 SCC 368
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
On consideration of the authorities about scope of Sections 227 and 228 of the Code, the following principles emerge:
(i) The Judge while considering the question of framing the charges under Section 227 of the Cr.P.C. has the undoubted power to sift and weigh the evidence for the limited purpose of finding out whether or not a prima facie case against the accused has been made out.

The test to determine prima facie case would depend upon the Mohit Chaudhary vs State on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143274493/
3 facts of each case.
(ii) Where the materials placed before the Court disclose grave suspicion against the accused which has not been properly explained, the Court will be fully justified in framing a charge and proceeding with the trial.

entities.text: Mohit Chaudhary vs State on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iii) The Court cannot act merely as a Post Office or a mouthpiece of the prosecution but has to consider the broad probabilities of the case, the total effect of the evidence and the documents produced before the Court, any basic infirmities etc.
However, at this stage, there cannot be a roving enquiry into the pros and cons of the matter and weigh the evidence as if he was conducting a trial.

(iv) If on the basis of the material on record, the Court could form an opinion that the accused might have committed offence, it can frame the charge, though for conviction the conclusion is required to be proved beyond reasonable doubt that the accused has committed the offence.
Criminal Revision No. 29/2024 (v) At the time of framing of the charges, the probative value of the material on record cannot be gone into but before framing a charge the Court must apply its judicial mind on the material placed on record and must be satisfied that the commission of offence by the accused was possible.
(vi) At the stage of Sections 227 and 228, the Court is required to evaluate the material and documents on record with a view to find out if the facts emerging therefrom taken at their face value discloses the existence of all the ingredients constituting the alleged offence.

For this limited purpose, sift the evidence as it cannot be expected even at that initial stage to accept all that the prosecution states as gospel truth even if it is opposed to common sense or the broad probabilities of the case.

(vii) If two views are possible and one of them gives rise to suspicion only, as distinguished from grave suspicion, the trial Judge will be empowered to discharge the accused and at this stage, he is not to see whether the trial will end in conviction or acquittal."

8. Hon'ble Apex Court Asim Shariff Vs. National Investigation Agency reported in (2019) 7 SCC 148,
has observed as under :
"18.

sentences.text:
Taking note of the exposition of law on the subject laid down by this Court, it is settled that the Judge while considering the question of framing charge under Section 227 CrPC in sessions cases(which is akin to Section 239 CrPC pertaining to warrant cases) has the undoubted power to sift and weigh the evidence for the Criminal Revision No. 29/2024 limited purpose of finding out whether or not a prima facie case against the accused has been made out; where the material placed before the Court discloses grave suspicion against the accused which has not been properly Mohit Chaudhary vs State on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143274493/
4 explained, the Court will be fully justified in framing the charge; by and large if two views are possible and one of them giving rise to suspicion only, as distinguished from grave suspicion against the accused, the trial Judge will be justified in discharging him.

entities.text: Mohit Chaudhary vs State on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is thus clear that while examining the discharge application filed under Section 227 CrPC, it is expected from the trial Judge to exercise its judicial mind to determine as to whether a case for trial has been made out or not.

It is true that in such proceedings, the Court is not supposed to hold a mini trial by marshalling the evidence on record."
9.

On the aspect of standard of proof at the stage of charge, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Bhawna Bai v. Ghanshyam reported in (2020) 2 SCC 217, has observed as under :
13.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ...At the time of framing the charges, only prima facie case is to be seen; whether case is beyond reasonable doubt, is not to be seen at this stage.
At the stage of framing the charge, the court has to see if there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.
While evaluating the materials, strict standard of proof is not required; only prima facie case against the accused is to be seen Criminal Revision No. 29/2024 10.

Reverting to the present matter, the main thrust of argument advanced by revisionists is that the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate the entire facts of the case and material available on record and directed to frame charge mentioned as above against the revisionists/petitioners.
11. After analysing the material available on record, Ld. Trial Court vide impugned order while directing the framing of charge against the accused persons

has observed that :
"Perusal of the record shows that complainant in her complaint dated 27.12.2017 has stated that she got married to accused Mohit Chaudhary on 26.02.2014, wherein her parents spent Rs.30 Lakhs according to the demands of accused & his parents & also gave cash, gold jewellery & customary gifts.

Complainant has alleged that when she &
her father asked Mohit about his job, he falsely mentioned about his work, earnings,
financial status & family background.
Complainant has alleged that after her ring ceremony, accused Mohit demanded five star hotel for stay of baratis & he & his father always demanded a Hyundai Creta Car from her parents.
Complainant has alleged that her parents-in-law & accused Mohit always harassed & tortured her for not bringing the car in dowry & her mother-in-law alongwith sister-in-law openly taunted her.

Complainant has alleged that she handed over all her jewellery to Criminal Revision No. 29/2024 her husband & parents-in-law on the pretext of keeping them safe & same has not been returned to her till date despite repeated demands.

She has further alleged that soon after the marriage, she found the behaviour of her husband & in-laws cruel & indifferent towards her & her parents as they did not fulfill their demand of Hyundai Creta & also started to put demands on her & showed dissatisfaction on the quantity & quality of articles given in dowry and also tortured her physically by slapping & punching in abdomen, they also made Mohit Chaudhary vs State on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143274493/

5 sarcastic remarks, taunted complainant,used filthy language for her parents,
sometimes had to beg for food and was also humiliated & physically tortured by accused persons even in presence of guests.

Complainant has further alleged that on 06.03.2014, accused Mohit abused her,
slapped her in front of mob & also threatened her.
On 15.03.2014, accused Mohit slapped & punched her, pulled her by hair, threw her on bed and forcibly committed unnatural intercourse with her.

On 11.10.2014, her mother-in-law & sister-in-law threatened her when she complained about accused Mohit & asked her not to talk to him, not to have child & also slapped her and on 19.10.2014, while complainant was cleaning the house standing on chair, they pulled the chair & made her fall.
She further alleged that one day, Criminal Revision No. 29/2024 her mother-in-law also threw tea on her face & punched on her back.

Complainant further alleged that when she went to Amritsar at matrimonial home, her father-in-law asked her to get money transferred & she was forced to give them Rs.90,000/- for buying household articles and when she visited Chandigarh/Mohali with Mohit her parents were forced to meet his demands and purchased him things such as LED, AC etc.
On 14.03.2015, accused Mohit again demanded unnatural intercourse & when complainant refused, he got physically and sexually abusive and tried to choke her with his hands.
Complainant has further alleged that during Holi on 05.03.1025, her father-in-law took her to a corner, touched her inappropriately on face & breasts and also tried to force her inside a room.

She further alleged that on 13.12.2015, her father-in-law asked her to make compromise & tried to get physical with her, he touched her private parts &
molested her.
In her statement recorded u/s 164 Cr.P.C. also complainant has made similar allegations against accused persons.

12. Keeping in view the allegations levelled by the complainant veracity to which shall be tested during the trial as well as applying the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex to the present case, this Court does not find any mitigating circumstances to interfere Criminal Revision No. 29/2024 with the impugned order.
Accordingly, present criminal revision petition is dismissed being bereft of any merit.
13. The trial Court record along with the copy of this order be sent back to the learned Trial Court.
14. The file of this revision petition be consigned to record room after due compliance.
